newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil lower in Europe after export data.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil lower in Europe after export data.

text.p: Palm oil prices were lower at midday in Europe on Monday on the back of bearish Malaysian palm oil export data.

Malaysian cargo surveyor SGS put local exports during June at 611,368 tonnes against 672,805 tonnes in May. Traders in Asia said the figures were within expectations but European players said they were not supportive.
Further data is expected on Tuesday from cargo surveyor Caleb Brett.
Soft oils were higher despite new contract lows at the close of the Chicago soy futures on Friday.
Traders said the market was thin with prices boosted partly by the stronger dollar and some local tightness in supplies.
"Sellers have not been very keen this morning and even if they had been there were not many buyers about anyway," said one trader.
At midday crude palm oil cif Europe was $5 down after Jul traded at $520 and Aug/Dec at $520 a tonne cif.
RBD palm oil fetched $505 a tonne for Jul while $540 and $537.50 a tonne was paid for olein and $535 a tonne fob Malaysian ports for Oct/Dec. Refined palm oil sellers were $5 to $7.50 down.
Among soft oils soy oil was one guilder up and rape oil 0.50 to 0.75 guilders higher.
Lauric oils were mixed with coconut oil $5 up to unchanged and palmkernel oil unchanged to $2.50 down with buyers nowhere to be seen.
